identification.summary: UAC-0245 is a CERT-UA tracking identifier for a threat cluster that CERT-UA reported in late September / early October 2025 for targeted attacks in Ukraine using a C-based backdoor named CABINETRAT, delivered as malicious Excel XLL add-ins inside ZIP archives shared over Signal [S2][S3]. Press coverage describes the targets as Ukrainian government and defense organizations [S4].
identification.firstObserved: Activity observed September 2025 per CERT-UA as reported by secondary sources [S2][S3].
identification.notes: UAC-0xxx is CERT-UA's uncategorized-cluster naming scheme, not a vendor name; no Microsoft name or other vendor alias was found in the sources gathered. SOC Prime reports CERT-UA#17479 as the advisory tag [S5]. The CERT-UA primary page could not be verified, so all technical detail below comes from secondary coverage.

attribution.basis: None of the reviewed coverage attributes UAC-0245 to a named state or organization [S2][S3]. Reporting only notes that XLL files were previously seen in UAC-0002 (Sandworm/APT44) attacks on Ukrainian critical infrastructure, which is a tooling comparison and not an attribution [S5]. Bitdefender's headline coverage characterizes the group as Russian-linked [S4]; this is the outlet's characterization, not a government or CERT-UA attribution.

objectives: Not stated by sources. CABINETRAT functionality (system information, installed-program listing, screenshots, file operations, command execution) is consistent with reconnaissance and data collection [S2][S3].

targeting.notes: Sectors per Bitdefender's description of Ukrainian government and defense organizations [S4]; CERT-UA warning concerned attacks on the Defense Forces (per secondary coverage) [S2][S3]. The lure was a document about detention of persons who attempted to cross the Ukrainian border [S2][S3].

capabilities.summary: Delivery by ZIP archives shared over Signal containing a malicious XLL Excel add-in (one reported archive name 500.zip with dodatok.xll) [S2][S3]. The XLL drops an EXE in the Startup folder, an XLL named BasicExcelMath.xll in %APPDATA%, and a PNG named Office.png, modifies the registry for persistence, launches Excel hidden with the /e parameter, and extracts shellcode from the PNG [S2][S3]. Reports also describe randomized Run-key entries and a scheduled task running every 12 hours [S5]. CABINETRAT is a C-language backdoor that gathers system information, installed programs and screenshots, enumerates directories, deletes files, runs commands, and uploads/downloads files over a TCP connection to a remote server [S2][S3]. Loader and shellcode check for at least 2 CPU cores, 3 GB RAM and virtualization products (VMware, VirtualBox, Xen, QEMU, Parallels, Hyper-V) to evade analysis [S2][S3].

campaigns.name: CABINETRAT campaign against Ukrainian defense/government targets
campaigns.summary: CERT-UA observed Signal-delivered ZIP archives with XLL add-ins that deploy the CABINETRAT backdoor, using a border-detention document lure [S2][S3][S4].

campaigns.name: CERT-UA public warning
campaigns.summary: CERT-UA publicized the activity and the UAC-0245 identifier (advisory tag CERT-UA#17479 per SOC Prime) [S2][S5].

diamond.adversary: Unattributed cluster tracked by CERT-UA as UAC-0245 [S2][S3].
diamond.capability: XLL Excel add-in loader, PNG-hidden shellcode, CABINETRAT C backdoor, anti-VM checks [S2][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Signal messenger used to distribute ZIP archives; backdoor communicates with a remote server over TCP [S2][S3]. Specific C2 addresses not captured.
diamond.technology: Windows with Microsoft Excel (XLL add-in loading) and Signal as a delivery channel [S2][S3].

gaps: CERT-UA primary advisory could not be verified; all details are from secondary coverage and artifact names vary between reports.
No state or organizational attribution found; Russian link is only a media characterization [S4].
No vendor alias or MITRE group mapping found; overlap with other CERT-UA clusters (e.g. UAC-0002) is not established, only a shared XLL technique noted [S5].
IOCs (hashes, C2 addresses), victim counts and confidence statements not captured.
No later UAC-0245 activity found in searches through 2026-10.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Personal and unofficial messaging channels (Signal) and Office add-in loading are exposure points for defense personnel; endpoints running Excel are key terrain [S2][S3]. STEP 2: Adversary reaches personnel outside managed email gateways using a topical lure [S2][S3]. STEP 3: Template is Signal-delivered ZIP, XLL add-in, PNG shellcode, persistence via Startup, Run key and scheduled task, then C-based RAT with screenshot and file collection [S2][S3][S5]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued targeted compromise of Ukrainian defense and government users for collection; MDCOA is the same XLL/Signal vector turned against coalition or partner defense personnel. Candidate indicators: XLL files within ZIPs received over messaging apps, Excel launched hidden with /e, BasicExcelMath.xll in %APPDATA%, Office.png, new Startup-folder EXEs, 12-hour scheduled tasks [S2][S3][S5].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track CERT-UA UAC-series advisories and ingest artifact names above into hunt content. (2) Authorities: policy on personal messaging apps and blocking XLL/Office add-in execution requires commander and DAA decisions. (3) Mission assurance: restrict add-in loading and block ZIPs with XLL content on managed endpoints. (4) Coordination: share indicators with partner CERTs and DC3; because attribution is open, prioritize containment over naming.
